html:
SMTO-GML-0040 — SMTO lost its connection to Gmail

GUID: a8aad437-8c57-44ce-8155-98a4088b78a8
Slug: gmail-provider-transport-failed
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The connection between SMTO and Google broke before Gmail answered. A lost connection doesn't prove the request failed; a send or change may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is online and can open Google websites such as gmail.com. SMTO needs a working network path to Google to reach your mailbox.
  2. If you're on a work network or VPN, ask your network administrator whether Google is blocked or goes through a proxy. Firewalls and proxies commonly cut these connections.
  3. If the Task was sending or changing email, check Sent, Drafts or Trash in Gmail to see whether it already happened. The connection may have broken after Google received the request, so it may have been done anyway.
  4. Then ask SMTO again in the conversation, only for what is still missing. Asking only for missing work avoids sending the same email twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the Gmail request, and each email or change appears in Gmail only once.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking again. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off secure-connection checks to make it work, and don't resend anything without checking Sent first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail API or Google OAuth request failed with a connection-level or operating-system network error (ConnectionError or OSError) before a complete response was received.

What this means

  • The native capability catches a connection/OS transport error after its unknown-write guard, and selects the provider-transport category. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The native capability catches a connection/OS transport error after its unknown-write guard, and selects the provider-transport category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect concrete DNS/proxy/TLS/connection evidence before choosing a network repair.

How to fix it

  • Check DNS resolution, proxy settings, firewall rules and TLS interception between the Server and gmail.googleapis.com / oauth2.googleapis.com (for app-password accounts, between the paired Gateway and imap.gmail.com:993 / smtp.gmail.com:587). Do not disable TLS verification. Before repeating a write, inspect the live mailbox for the earlier effect.
  • Check network, DNS, proxy and TLS connectivity to the intended Google endpoint. Reconcile any uncertain write against provider state before repeating it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended transport route works and any earlier write uncertainty is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
